params.textField: It is important to treat asthma, because it is a chronic inflammatory disorder and as such may result in permanent damage to the lungs over time. While one would hypothesise that *antihistamines* would be useful in asthma, most asthmatics do not get relief from them, although some asthmatics may have slight overall improvements over time, from prophylactic treatment. Treatment of an acute asthmatic attack is normally going to involve a short acting Beta 2 agonist like *salbutamol*, or if the person is not tolerant of that, an anticholinergic bronchodilator like *ipratropium* could be used. If those are being used more frequently than about 4 times per week, there is often an inclusion of a corticosteroid like *budesonide* or fluticasone. This is often accompanied by a long acting Beta 2 agonist like *salmeterol*. If the asthma is not controlled with strong inhaled corticosteroids, there may need to be an inclusion of an oral corticosteroid like *prednisone*. Other drugs that may be helpful include the (oral; PO) leukotriene receptor antagonists like *montelukast* that block some of the potent mediators of inflammation that play a big role in the inflammation associated with asthma.
